messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert triggered on smart-routing: sudden spike in 5xxs + model-variant mismatch metric (smart.router.variant_mismatch > 4% over 5m). Paging @oncall-sam and @oncall-lee. Details: https://ops.redwood/alerts/1951230123
oncall-sam: ack. I'm on it. grabbing tracing and recent routing policy diffs.
prod-eng-dan: noticed increased fallback chaining between us-west and eu-west starting ~10m ago. we had a routing policy tweak earlier to broaden compatible-variants set (policy id RP-811).
eng-rita: looking at KV cache traces now. router is returning cached kv for key `route_kv:eu-west:customer:890:model=gpt-medium` to requests that explicitly asked for `gpt-medium-v3` and `gpt-medium-v2`. some downstream hosts treat v2/v3 as incompatible but cache payload is variant-specific.
oncall-lee: are keys including variant? sample: `route_kv:eu-west:customer:890:model=gpt-medium` (no variant or build id). that explains reuse.
support-maya: customer 890 flagged us — they got older model outputs and raised a P1. two other customers in eu-west also reporting wrong outputs.
eng-rita: digging: RP-811 introduced a compatibility normalization that collapsed variant suffixes to boost cache reuse across micro-variants. it also enabled cross-region fallback to read from sibling-region cache when local miss. combo = wrong variant served from sibling region.
oncall-sam: mitigation plan proposals: A) toggle smart-routing to strict-variant-match (fail safe) — instant but reduces cache hits. B) rollback RP-811 normalization (needs deploy, ~6-8m). C) temporarily disable cross-region cache reads (config flip, ~2m). D) surgical delete of keys that lack variant id for impacted customer namespaces (risky but fast).
prod-eng-dan: prefer C + A as quick protective change, then B as durable fix. delete only after config flips to prevent re-population.
eng-rita: agree. I'll flip `router.strict_variant_matching=true` and disable `router.cross_region_cache_reads=false` for eu-west.
config-bot: config-change-bot: applying change to routers in eu-west: `router.strict_variant_matching=true`
config-bot: config-change-bot: applying change to routers in eu-west: `router.cross_region_cache_reads=false`
config-bot: config-change-bot: reload completed on 6 routers (eu-west).
oncall-lee: monitoring metrics. variant_mismatch alert falling from 4.8% to 1.2% in 3m. 5xxs also trending down.
support-maya: notifying impacted customers: "We're investigating and have applied mitigation that should stop incorrect model responses. We'll follow up with timeline and RCA."
prod-eng-dan: starting rollback plan for RP-811 in parallel. will kick off canary rollback first. deploy-bot: starting rollback job rb-2011 for RP-811 canary.
deploy-bot: rollback job rb-2011 initiated. canary target: 10% traffic.
oncall-sam: good. start preparing a safe scan-delete script that only removes keys without variant token and only for customers flagged as impacted. Script will be manual interactive. Example preview command: ```redis-cli -h redis-eu --scan --pattern 'route_kv:eu-west:customer:890:*' | grep -v 'variant=' > /tmp/keys-no-variant.txt```
eng-rita: note: keys lacking variant may be used by healthy requests too; hence we must prevent writer from re-creating malformed keys. I'll patch router write path to include variant immediately (hot config) before we delete.
config-bot: applying config: `router.append_variant_on_write=true` to eu-west routers.
config-bot: reload succeeded.
noncall-lee: canary rollback for RP-811 completed. metrics for canary show no regressions; starting full rollback.
deploy-bot: rollback job rb-2011 completed (global).
eng-rita: with strict matching and cross-region reads off, variant_mismatch is now under 0.3%. proceeding with interactive scan/delete for customers 890, 452, 233. running list-only first.
support-maya: customers 890 and 452 confirm improved outputs in tickets #9982 and #9985.
noncall-sam: deleting keys older than 30m that lack variant id for customer 890: command pattern used: ```redis-cli -h redis-eu --scan --pattern 'route_kv:eu-west:customer:890:*' | while read k; do ttl=$(redis-cli -h redis-eu ttl "$k"); if [[ "$ttl" -lt 0 ]]; then echo "$k has no ttl"; fi; # manual check; done``` Deleting ~85 keys after manual review.
eng-rita: watch CPU and p99 latency during deletes. we rate-limit deletes to 200/s.
noncall-lee: after deletes, immediate drop in wrong-variant traces for customer 890.
support-maya: customer 233 still reporting intermittent issue; looks like their traffic routed via us-west sibling region earlier. checking keys there.
prod-eng-dan: discovered some stale cross-region replication that left variant-less keys in us-west with eu-west TTLs. engaging infra to sweep only affected namespaces.
eng-rita: infra ran a regional-only sweep for the three customers in us-west, removing ~620 keys.
config-bot: router config already ensures new writes include variant.
noncall-sam: impact summary so far: 9 customers affected, 3 escalated to P1, estimated 3.2k bad responses over 28m window. main cause: RP-811 normalization + cross-region cache reads combined to serve wrong cached payloads across similar model aliases.
prod-eng-dan: follow-ups: (1) revert normalization permanently (RP-811 removal) ✅, (2) change cache key schema to explicitly include variant+build+region (task INF-933), (3) add pre-deploy invariant checker that validates new routing key format won't drop tokens (task INF-934), (4) add an automated canary that verifies variant fidelity on real requests for 10m window post deploy (task INF-935).
noncall-lee: handing over to @oncall-lee for recovery ops and postmortem ownership. Sam remains incident comms lead.
noncall-lee: taking postmortem. I'll draft timeline and RCA. Preliminary timeline: detect T0, mitigation config flips at T+4m, canary rollback started T+7m, full rollback T+12m, KV cleanup and cross-region sweep T+20m, resolved T+34m.
support-maya: customers notified of fix. will keep monitoring and update customers when postmortem ready.
incident-bot: incident closed by oncall-lee. Severity downgraded to SEV3; follow-ups assigned to INF-933, INF-934, INF-935.
noncall-sam: thanks all. notes: quick config flips saved us from broader impact. postmortem draft incoming in #postmortems. :raised_hands:
